_comment: Comment corpus for warming. Used by warm skills when planning a 'comment' action against another user's post. Skills read this; the user edits it.

_authoring_rules.no_terminal_punctuation: skip periods/exclamation marks — they read formal/bot. Apostrophes inside words are fine (god's / he's).
_authoring_rules.no_self_promo: never reference Swift Bible, the app, or am2.biz in a comment
_authoring_rules.voice: casual social-native, devotional + encouraging. Brief enough that repetition isn't immediately obvious.

_usage.selection: Skills sample one phrase per planned comment action. Default category is 'universal'. Future: detect target-post theme (verse / testimony / teaching / praise) and pick from the matching category.
anti_pattern_safeguards: Do NOT use the same phrase twice within 7 days against the same platform.
Do NOT comment on the same author within 30 days.
Do NOT comment + like + save on the same post in one pass — pick at most ONE engagement per target post.
Skip any candidate post whose author handle includes 'bible' or 'swiftbible' (might be us or a parody).

Skip any target whose visible text matches a reply-prompt pattern: /reply with/i, /comment .{1,15} below/i, /type ["']?[A-Za-z]{2,12}["']?/i, /say .{1,20} below/i. These posts expect a specific keyword (often 'amen' or a verse reference) and a generic corpus phrase will look obviously off. Set 2026-05-05 after our first X test landed 'blessed' on a tweet whose image said 'reply with amen' — the user had to delete the reply manually.
Lean on captions/alt-text for image-based prompts when available — a fully-image-driven prompt won't surface in tweetText. If alt-text isn't accessible, prefer to skip rather than guess.
_usage.track_used: When a comment is posted, append the phrase + platform + target post id + timestamp to ~/.social-agents/state/comment-history.json so the de-dup checks above can run.
